briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Trophies, Deals and a Court Win: Cannabis Momentum Builds From Pontiac to D.C.
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis scene closed out the week with hardware, headlines and a governor's race that's suddenly all about tax relief, even as the 24% wholesale tax keeps squeezing margins. Nationally, the mood is bullish: a federal court just protected marijuana rescheduling, Eli Lilly bought its way into psychedelics, and the first FDA-approved psilocybin drug is inching toward a 2027 launch.

local.text: Mitten Canna, Hytek crowned Michigan's cannabis champs — Mitten Canna Co.'s Toad Venom took best overall flower and Hytek's Oishii Piña won best overall rosin at the fifth annual Zalympix, announced at the Crofoot in Pontiac.

Jars Cannabis clears a path in Madison Heights — the 54-store chain reached a deal to remove a Flock surveillance camera that had been aimed at its parking lot, closing out a lingering condition from a 2022 licensing lawsuit settlement.

Tax relief becomes a 2026 campaign flashpoint — State Sen. Jeff Irwin is warning the industry not to trust GOP gubernatorial candidate John James, whom top cannabis executives recently endorsed over his pledge to cut the 24% wholesale weed tax.

Menominee voters could add four dispensary licenses — a ballot measure this week asks whether to raise the city's cap from nine stores to 13, a year after the original cap touched off a wave of licensing lawsuits.

Distressed cannabis real estate is going cheap — at least 50 Michigan cannabis properties are now listed for sale or lease, with brokers reporting deals closing at 20 to 30 cents on the dollar, an opening for well-capitalized operators to expand.

national.text: Federal court keeps marijuana rescheduling on track — the D.C. Circuit rejected a challenge to the medical-marijuana Schedule III shift on Sept. 9, leaving the reclassification in effect as the DEA's broader recreational rescheduling case remains pending.

FDA lays groundwork for psychedelic drug approvals — the agency's new September framework reshapes trial design and safety requirements for psilocybin and MDMA therapies, building on its Sept. 14 public hearing on psychedelic medicine.

First psilocybin drug nears the finish line — Compass Pathways expects to complete its rolling FDA submission for COMP360 in Q4, with a potential U.S. launch in the first half of 2027, after landing a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher.

Eli Lilly buys its way into psychedelics — Lilly's acquisition of atai/Beckley assets, bringing BPL-003, VLS-01 and EMP-01 into its pipeline, closed Sept. 11, marking big pharma's arrival in the sector.

Cannabis MSOs keep consolidating — Vireo Growth's all-stock deal for Planet 13 adds 36 dispensaries and pushes the combined company toward roughly 265 stores across 15 states, one of the largest retail footprints in the U.S.
